items.title: AI auditors catch most agent misbehavior but flood reviewers with false alarms, new study finds
items.summary: AI models can often spot problematic behavior by other AI agents in logs, according to a study by Anthropic researcher Andy Hall. GPT-5 found about 98 percent of reward-hacking cases, but the more exhaustively the search is tuned, the more false alarms pile up. That's not yet enough for reliable safety checks....

items.title: AI coding agents still need human cleanup on nearly three out of four tasks in a real-world test
items.summary: Alibaba's new coding-agent benchmark, Co-Design Bench, tests AI agents on real user requests that already tripped them up in practice. Even GPT-6 Astra, the top performer, fully solves only 26.4 percent of tasks. On older benchmarks, the same models score above 99 percent. The article AI coding agents still need human cleanup on nearly three out of four tasks in a real-world test appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: The gap between open and closed AI models in cyber capabilities keeps shrinking
items.summary: In the Vals AI benchmark, OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol Daybreak hits 80.8 percent of attack objectives in simulated corporate networks. Worse, the open-weight model DeepSeek V4.1 Flash reaches 72.8 percent at a tenth of the cost. Because open models can no longer be restricted, analysts say the window for defenders is shrinking fast....

items.title: The inventor of the bitter lesson has a bitter lesson for LLM scaling enthusiasts
items.summary: Turing Award winner Richard Sutton reaffirms that raw compute alone isn't enough for intelligence and that fundamentally new learning methods are needed. Ex-OpenAI researcher Tworek agrees, saying blind transformer scaling "has reward hacked brains of a whole generation of scientists." A growing wave of startups is already betting on exactly this gap....

items.title: Partnering with Hacktron to find vulnerabilities in OpenAI’s systems
items.summary: OpenAI is partnering with Hacktron to find vulnerabilities, test connections with third-party services, and strengthen defenses with frontier AI.

items.title: Megaspeed exec was recruited to spy on Nvidia CEO, according to US intelligence memo
items.summary: A memo circulated earlier this year reportedly claimed that China’s Ministry of State Security recruited a female technology executive to spy on Nvidia's CEO.

items.title: Nvidia will investigate CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with possible Chinese spy
items.summary: In a memo to the company, Huang admitted that he had an affair.

items.title: How Grab Improved Mobile App Stability by Safely Handling Surge in AI-Generated Code Changes
items.summary: The growing adoption of AI coding assistants has accelerated development and increased the volume of code changes per release, bringing more opportunities for defects and crashes, says Grab. To address these challenges, they implemented a layered defense strategy to prevent, detect, and contain crashes throughout the development and release lifecycle. By Sergio De Simone

items.title: OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
items.summary: OpenAI has reportedly raised an additional $11 billion as part of a funding round that hasn't closed yet but is expected to in the coming weeks.

items.title: Ramp data shows AI spending stalling just as Anthropic nears its IPO
items.summary: AI usage keeps climbing, but spending has stalled. Price cuts and smarter cost controls among the biggest spenders could challenge investor assumptions about AI hypergrowth.

items.title: Open Source pg_vectorsearch Brings More Scalable Vector Search to PostgreSQL
items.summary: Tiger Data has released pg_vectorsearch, an open source PostgreSQL extension for vector similarity search, currently in alpha. Its PRISM index uses data partitioning and compression instead of the graph-based approach used by pgvector’s HNSW index, reducing memory requirements and index build times. By Renato Losio
